evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/onboarding/FeedbackManager.ts:138-140 — `getDrafts()` does `const stored = await AsyncStorage.getItem(FEEDBACK_DRAFTS_KEY); return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : [];` with NO try/catch. A corrupted / partially-written FEEDBACK_DRAFTS_KEY blob (interrupted write, schema drift across an app update, manual storage tampering) makes JSON.parse throw, and the throw propagates to the caller (the feedback draft-loading flow in screens/help/FeedbackScreen.tsx) rather than degrading to an empty list.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/onboarding/FeedbackManager.ts:229-231 — `getPendingFeedback()` has the identical unguarded pattern on PENDING_FEEDBACK_KEY: `return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : [];`. This is called by `retryPendingFeedback()` (line 161) and `storePendingFeedback()` (line 233); a corrupted blob throws and silently aborts the offline-feedback retry/enqueue path, so queued feedback can be neither retried nor added until storage is cleared.

Divergence from the codebase's own established defensive convention IN THE SAME DIRECTORY: onboarding/TourManager.ts:277-294 and onboarding/HelpCenter.ts:191-199 both wrap their AsyncStorage JSON.parse in try/catch and reset-to-default with a `console.warn('... corrupted ... resetting to default')`; nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts:224/353/363 does the same ('Stored ... corrupted; discarding'). FeedbackManager is the outlier that never adopted the pattern. The sibling WidgetDataProvider instances of this same class are already tracked (code-review-mobile-rn-widget-parse-unguarded, code-review-mobile-rn-widget-storage-unguarded-jsonparse) but FeedbackManager was never flagged — the 2026-09-17 onboarding/ review only examined FeedbackManager.submitFeedback (confirmed not-a-bug) and did not reach getDrafts/getPendingFeedback.

Net-new verification: grep of backlog.json + all prior mobile-rn signal files for FeedbackManager/getDrafts/getPendingFeedback/FEEDBACK_DRAFTS/PENDING_FEEDBACK parse shows the only FeedbackManager finding on record is code-review-mobile-rn-feedback-device-info-i18n (an i18n gap, different concern). No prior finding covers the unguarded-parse resilience gap in this file.

Severity LOW (+1): no happy-path crash and no data loss on normal operation; impact is confined to the corrupted-storage edge, and feedback is a non-critical surface. Confidence medium (static-only: the throw-on-corruption is certain by inspection, but triggering it requires a corrupted blob that cannot be produced in the cloud runner). Cloud-landable frontend-only fix: wrap both reads in try/catch returning `[]` on parse failure (and optionally `console.warn` + delete the corrupted key), mirroring TourManager/HelpCenter. Fix both sites in one PR.
